quality_guards: A fixed testing interval is not suitable for every item or workplace; the risk assessment and evidence history matter.
Electrical guidance is operational safety context and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
The proportionate control depends on the task, duration, surface, access method and foreseeable rescue needs.
Work-at-height guidance is task-specific context and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
The responsible person must be competent and have sufficient resources, skills, training and authority.
Asbestos evidence is building- and material-specific and is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
Temperature targets and monitoring frequency depend on system design, occupancy and risk assessment.
Legionella guidance is water-system-specific context and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
The indicative radon map is a screening tool and address-specific measurement may still be required.
Radon evidence is location- and building-specific and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
A precautionary allergen statement should not replace effective segregation, cleaning and risk control.
Allergen safety is product-, recipe- and process-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
A product alert applies only to the identified product, model, batch or risk scope and should not be generalised.
Product recall evidence is item-specific and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
Flood-warning lead times and affected areas depend on current forecasts, catchment conditions, tides and local observations.
Flood-warning evidence is dynamic and must not be treated as a permanent parcel-level probability.
Official-source context is not converted into exact parcel-level probability.
